result.summary: 2025 was a busy year for dated Altman predictions. His own essays (Three Observations, The Gentle Singularity, and OpenAI's 'Ten years' post) put markers on 2026, 2027, 2030, the 2030s and 2035, ending with superintelligence 'almost certain' within ten years. In interviews he bet on an AI-driven significant discovery by late 2027 (Cleo Abram) and said he would be very surprised not to have models beyond human ability by 2030 (Axel Springer/POLITICO); the Sequoia AI Ascent roadmap was seen only in a Claude-written summary, and the December Big Technology Podcast transcript could not be opened.

reply_text:
I found seven new dated AI predictions Altman made in 2025, plus two lines that are already in your files. The strongest come from his own writing and from printed interviews:
- **"Ten years" (OpenAI, 11 December):** he believes OpenAI is "almost certain to build superintelligence" within ten more years.
- **Axel Springer / POLITICO interview (25 September):** he said he'd be "very surprised" if models that "do things that we ourselves cannot do" don't exist by 2030.
- **Cleo Abram podcast (8 August):** he bet that by late 2027 most people will agree AI has made a significant new discovery.

Things you should check:
- **Blog dates:** The blog front page I opened doesn't print post dates. The February date for "Three Observations" is from my memory, not the page. The 10 June date for "The Gentle Singularity" matches your existing file.
- **Cleo Abram transcript:** This is a third-party transcript, not an official one. It has some likely mishearings, for example "early 2025" next to "late 2026, sorry, early 2026".
- **Sequoia AI Ascent (May):** The only page I saw is Sequoia's own post, and it says Claude wrote it from the talk transcript. Treat the quoted words as coverage only. They predict the same 2026 and 2027 steps as your 10 June files, but this is a separate, earlier occasion. I left `already_recorded` empty for these.
- **Big Technology Podcast (December):** The transcript page was blocked (url_not_allowed), so I quote nothing from it. News reports say Altman linked "perfect memory" in AI to 2026, but I couldn't confirm his words.

I ran 9 of the 12 searches. I didn't use the last 3 because all 6 page openings were spent, and I don't quote from search snippets.
